prism-designframe · v0.99

Designframe is the D in MVCD.

A Display layer separated from Model / View / Controller — designed so engineers don't make design decisions, and end users can customize UI without designer or engineer skills. Two audiences, one solution: math + structural defaults that propagate intent without breaking layout.

Minimalist

No choice that isn't necessary. Every customization option is a maintenance cost; every removal sharpens intent.

Adaptive

Survives across every viewport without manual tuning. Math + structural defaults propagate; consumers don't re-author responsive variants.

Semantic

HTML elements carry meaning; classes never override that. The cascade rewards correct semantics; punishes div-soup.

Resilient

Composed by AI, junior engineers, and non-designers without producing broken layouts. The framework's defaults are the safe path.

Identity · 1.1

Brand assets

Logo lockups, marks, and favicons that ship with the system. Replace asset files when forking; usage rules below propagate to consumers via PRISM.md.

logo.primary

assets/logos/df-wordmark.svg

Default lockup for light surfaces. Maintain clear-space equal to space.gutter.base on all sides. Minimum height 24px for legibility. Don't recolor — the wordmark is intentionally monochromatic; color treatments dilute the identity. Don't outline, drop-shadow, or apply effects. Don't stretch non-uniformly. For dark surfaces, switch to the on-dark variant (white letterforms, same geometry).

logo.mark

Designframe mark — three solid circles of decreasing size, aligned on the horizontal centerline of a 1024×1024 square canvas. The default variant places white circles on a

assets/logos/df-mark.svg

Use when wordmark length is constrained (app tile, social avatar, square thumbnail, top-nav lockup). The mark canvas is a true square — don't apply corner radius; the flat geometry is a deliberate identity choice (the brand-mark squareness is asset-side, independent of radius.brand.corner which applies to containers). Default variant: white circles on #222222 canvas. On-dark variant: #222222 circles on white canvas (use against dark surfaces). Minimum size 32px square — below that the three-circle scale hierarchy becomes visually indistinct; use logo.favicon instead.

logo.favicon

Designframe favicon — the three-circle mark inscribed in a full-bleed white circle. Geometrically the same motif as logo.mark but bounded by a circular outline rather than the square canvas, sized for 16-32px browser-tab and PWA-icon contexts where a circular mask is common.

Reserved for contexts where the square logo.mark canvas doesn't fit a target surface's icon mask (browser tabs, OS app dock, system notification badges that crop to a circular mask). At any size where logo.mark renders cleanly within its container, prefer logo.mark — the favicon is a mask-shape adaptation, not a scale-down alternative.

Section 2

Anatomy

A Designframe design system has three structural layers. Tokens carry the visual property values; structure defines the grammar that composes them; assets reference files that consumers embed. Forking the system means replacing brand-owned values; system-owned values stay stable across all consumers.

Brand-owned surface

Values consumers replace when adopting Designframe for their brand: color identity (key, primary, invert), typography families, brand-radii. Marked $brand-owned: true in PRISM.md.

  • color.brand.* and color.brand-alt.*
  • typography.family.{heading, body, display}
  • radius.brand.{min, base, corner, field}
  • color.theme.{header, footer}.*

System-owned surface

Values stable across all consumers — the framework's structural commitments. Marked $system-owned: true. Replacing these forks Designframe itself, not the brand.

  • space.* (gutter, shoulder, article, section, header, …)
  • typography.scale.* (d1–d3, h1–h6, p1–p5, nav, button, chip)
  • shadow.*, blur.*, border.*, transition.*
  • screen.* (breakpoints), layout.* (grid system)

Block hierarchy

The structural grammar consumers follow. Outside-in composition: container → context → blocks → content. Per df-rules.md §9, this hierarchy is enforced by the cascade — violating it produces unwanted space-y margins on semantic content.

html > body
  header > nav
  main
    section.theme.section-grid
      > div.block-* > content (hgroup / nav / stack / elements)
  footer > nav

Combo class pattern

Component styling composes via space-separated modifiers applied in a consistent order. Specificity escalates naturally as classes stack; no !important needed.

type . subtype . variant . style . size . shape . state

Example: .button.gradient.air.squared.lg.rounded.hover — each modifier raises specificity by one class-tier; the cascade resolves naturally.

Section 3

Color

Three tiers compose Designframe's color system: primitives (brand-owned literal values), semantic contexts ($ref pairs that name role: bg / fg / nav-link), and aliases (consumer-vocabulary $refs for MD3-style or shadcn-style consumers).

Replace these values when forking Designframe for a new brand. Every other color references these via $ref.

Accessibility

Every theme-context bg/fg pair passes WCAG-AA contrast at the appropriate threshold (4.5:1 body text; 3:1 large/display text). Saturated key-themed contexts carry $contrastTarget: large to declare their intended scale — body text on .theme.key automatically inverts via the cascade to maintain readability.

Section 4

Typography

Anchored on 16px base size + 24px line-height rhythm. Every step is a multiple or fraction of these anchors. Display steps (d1–d3, h1) use unitless line-height: 1; body + utility steps use absolute px values maintaining the 24px rhythm grid.

Section 5

Layout

Designframe has no T-shirt scale. Spacing is named by semantic context (gutter for section rhythm, shoulder for outer margin, article for card padding, etc.), and every context adapts across breakpoints via responsive utility classes (p-gutter, xl:p-gutter-xl). Removing T-shirt sizes removes a choice — engineers don't pick "md vs lg," they pick a context.

Adaptive spacing contexts

space.unit 4px
space.gutter 24px → 32px @xl
space.shoulder 24px → 40px @xl
space.section 48px → 64px @xl
space.article 16px → 24px @xl
space.element 16px
space.header 12px → 16px @xl
space.stack 16px
space.form 12px → 16px @xl
space.sub 8px → 12px @xl

Grid system

6 columns on mobile, 12 columns on desktop (lg+). The cascade switch happens at the screen.lg breakpoint (960px).

Section 7

Elevation

Three shadow tiers provide depth without committing to color overlay. box-shadow is a single property — setting it replaces any previous value, so use these tokens rather than authoring custom shadows alongside them.

shadow.light

0px 0px 4px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.125)

shadow.base

0px 2px 4px 0px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)

shadow.heavy

0px 4px 8px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)

Section 8

Modes

Designframe supports four orthogonal mode axes. Modes compose — .theme.alt.invert applies alt-palette darkness; .theme.key.alt applies alt key surface. Mode changes don't replace brand primitives; only the semantic-tier $ref targets reassign.

ModeClassWhat it changes
default(no class)Light mode + main brand palette. The cascade root.
dark / invert.theme.invertbg flips to primary (near-black); fg to invert (white). Cards auto-revert; buttons gradient-key-invert; shaders recalibrate.
alt.theme.altSwaps to alt brand palette (secondary identity, e.g. campaign mode).
key.theme.keySaturated key brand color as section bg. Components inside auto-invert (key↔invert swap on buttons, chips, form rings) to remain visible.

Try the mode toggle in the navigation to see how this page itself adopts each mode — the doc eats its own dogfood.

Section 9

Patterns

Designframe's cross-cutting conventions that aren't tokens but ARE the design system. These rules cannot be enforced by tokens alone — adopting them is part of adopting Designframe.

Variant vocabularies

Status indicators use one of two distinct vocabularies, never mixed:

  • Alert vocabulary (.notify, .success, .warning, .error) — for components signaling attention level or pass/fail state.
  • Lifecycle vocabulary (.active, .completed, .pending, .declined) — for components signaling entity lifecycle position.

A .badge uses alert vocab. A .status-dot uses lifecycle vocab. Mixing creates inconsistent mental models — and inconsistent product surfaces.

Semantic HTML mandate

Use semantic HTML directly (<section>, <article>, <header>, <footer>, <nav>, <hgroup>) — never wrap in decorative <div>s. block-* classes belong on wrapper <div>s (or <article> for self-contained content); putting them on <hgroup> or <nav> adds unwanted space-y margin between their children.

Button inner structure

All buttons require <span><p> inner structure for gradient border effects:

<a class="button gradient"><span><p>Button Text</p></span></a>

Icon-only buttons skip the <p> wrapper on the icon:

<a class="button icon gradient"><span><i class="fa-light fa-heart"></i></span></a>

Section 11

Resources

Downloads + source pointers. Each emitter outputs an artifact in its target ecosystem's native format; consumers pick what they need.

  • tailwind-preset.js — Tailwind v3+ preset (CJS module export). Install via presets: [require('./tailwind-preset.js')].
  • tokens.css — CSS custom properties with theme-class overlays. Single-file, drop-in.
  • df-input.css — DF source-form :root declarations (Quick Setup + Extended sections). Replaces the :root portion of an existing df-input.css.
  • figma-tokens-studio.json — Tokens Studio v2+ format with named sets per mode.
  • design-md.md — Google DESIGN.md with MD3 name crosswalk for the color tier.
  • tokens.json — Raw DTCG JSON (193 leaf tokens). Use with any DTCG-compatible tool or as the canonical pivot format. Paired with ./exports/rationale.md for AI-tooling upload (claude.ai/design).
